notes: Sales/AE notes: Pacific Bridge (PB) is evaluating Redwood Dedicated to replace an internal inference service that struggles at scale.
Business requirement: real-time customer chat (low-latency agent) + high-throughput embeddings for search re-rank.

Latency SLOs requested: p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 350ms for non-streaming short responses (<=128 tokens); streaming: time-to-first-token p50 <= 30ms, time-to-last-token targets depend on token count.

Measurement ambiguity: PB measures from client click-to-render (includes TLS/TCP/CDN/app overhead) while Redwood reports server-side 'response completion' and per-kv-cache token times. Need alignment.
Agreement suggestion: two parallel metrics sets - 'Client E2E' (PB SDK trace + Redwood server markers) and 'Server Completion' (Redwood per-request latency). Both p50/p95/p99 to be reported.
Streaming nuance: PB wants both TTF (time-to-first-token) and TTL (time-to-last-token) per message; also wants median inter-token spacing for long streams to detect stalls.

Measurement instrumentation: PB will add Redwood SDK hooks to emit spans for DNS/TCP/TLS/connect, request-send, first-token, last-token. Redwood to provide per-request timestamps (received, started, first_token_emitted, completed) in logs.

Throughput & reserved GPU planning: expected steady-state 500 concurrent active chats, average 8 TPS per GPU for chosen model under continuous batching; Redwood recommended 6 reserved GPUs for canary, with autoscale/burst policy to handle peaks.

SLA negotiation points: guaranteed p95 latency window, regional failover behavior, credits for sustained SLA misses (propose trial SLA during POC), and clear definition of measurement (whose clock/time sync counts).
Fallback and routing: PB requires automatic fallback to smaller quantized model in same pool on overload; also cross-region fallback acceptable with data residency caveats.
Cost sensitivity: PB targets unit cost reduction vs current self-host by 20% — Optimize suggestions (quantization + batching + prefix caching) to be included in proposal.
Quote from CTO on call: 'We need end-to-end reproducible numbers—if we can't agree on instrumentation we'll never sign the SLA.'
Operational ask: per-route dashboards in Redwood Console with token-level cost and per-request latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) plus raw trace download for audits.
POC plan: joint 72-hour load test with scripted streaming and non-streaming traces, compare client SDK traces to server-side logs, iterate on batch size and KV cache settings.
measurement_alignment: Define p50/p95/p99 explicitly: measured on server 'completion' timestamp by default; client E2E reported separately.
Streaming metrics: report time-to-first-token and time-to-last-token; include per-token inter-arrival statistics for p95 stall detection.
Client-side timing: PB SDK will capture DNS, TCP, TLS, request-send, first-byte, last-byte; map these to Redwood server markers during test using request-id correlation.
Clock sync: agree to use server-side timestamps as authoritative for SLA; client E2E used for UX monitoring and will have a known delta.
Test harness: use JMeter + custom streaming harness and Redwood-provided load agent; include TLS warm connections, keep-alive, and connection churn scenarios.
Reporting cadence: daily test reports during POC with p50/p95/p99 histograms, streaming TTF/TTL breakdowns, error rates, and GPU occupancy metrics.
